_readme: Hand-curated evaluation universe. Locked before any modelling (Stage 1) to
prevent scope creep and hindsight leakage.
Coordinates for the eight PDGL lakes are decoded from the ICIMOD/UNDP 2020
lake IDs, which encode the centroid: GL<lon*1000>E<lat*1000>N. So
GL086925E27898N = 86.925 E, 27.898 N. Source and verification in
Each lake carries a WINDOW, not just a point. Delineation searches the
window and takes the dominant water body, so a ~1 km coordinate error does
not silently produce a null result, and lakes are allowed to grow.
label_burst is the ground truth for recall. label_glof records whether the
event was a glacial lake outburst AT ALL. Chamoli is the case where those
two disagree, and that disagreement is the negative control.

lakes.name: Thyanbo Tsho (Thame)
lakes.why_it_matters: THE case. ~0.05 km2, below the 0.1 km2 Rounce et al. 2017 screening threshold, and stable 2017-2023. Growth-only screening misses it. Trigger was a rock/ice avalanche from an upper lake, not gradual growth.
lakes.coordinate_source: Bisht et al. 2025, Int. J. Disast. Studies Climate Resil. 1(2):65-76, states 27.83 N, 86.60 E

lakes.name: South Lhonak
lakes.why_it_matters: The opposite case: textbook area growth (0.11 km2 in 1962 to 1.69 km2 in 2023) that a growth screen WOULD flag. Used with Chamoli for threshold calibration; Nepal cases stay untouched.
lakes.coordinate_source: Wikipedia / Sattar et al. 2025 Science, 27 56 50.93 N, 88 19 53.54 E

lakes.name: Pyurepu supraglacial lake (Rasuwa / Lhende Khola)
lakes.why_it_matters: Transboundary AND supraglacial: invisible to a Nepal-only lake inventory and to moraine-dam analysis. Formed from ponds first seen Dec 2023 and drained in a single day.
lakes.coordinate_source: DHM/ICIMOD satellite analysis reported via Nepali press, Oct 2025: lat 28.4043, lon 85.6469, ~5150 m

lakes.name: Chamoli / Ronti Gad (NEGATIVE CONTROL)
lakes.why_it_matters: NOT a GLOF. ~27e6 m3 rock-and-ice avalanche from the north face of Ronti Peak, 200+ killed. A system that attributes this to lake growth is measuring the wrong thing. Used with South Lhonak for calibration.
lakes.coordinate_source: Ronti Peak, 30 22 09 N 79 43 10 E (Shugar et al. 2021 Science 373:300)

lakes.name: Imja Tsho
lakes.pdgl_note: Lake water lowered by 4 m in 2016; lake expansion reduced; ice underneath end moraine; merging of supraglacial pond
lakes.why_it_matters: Known-high positive by expert ranking, mitigated in 2016. Tests whether the model reproduces expert judgement without a burst label.
lakes.coordinate_source: ICIMOD/UNDP 2020 PDGL report, lake ID GL086925E27898N

lakes.name: Tsho Rolpa
lakes.pdgl_note: Lake water lowered in 2000; expanding rapidly with retreat of calving source glacier; steep moraine; side moraine thin and in danger; hanging lake in tributary glacier
lakes.why_it_matters: The EWS cautionary tale. ~USD 3.2M lowering plus a 19-village early warning system, completed 2000-2002, now defunct. Justifies the human-in-the-loop, low-bandwidth framing.
lakes.coordinate_source: ICIMOD/UNDP 2020 PDGL report, lake ID GL086476E27861N

lakes.name: Thulagi
lakes.why_it_matters: One of the six historically highly critical Nepal lakes; the only Gandaki-basin lake in the set, so it tests that the pipeline is not Koshi-specific.
lakes.coordinate_source: ICIMOD/UNDP 2020 PDGL report, lake ID GL084485E28488N

lakes.name: Lower Barun
lakes.pdgl_note: Possibility of lake expansion; calving source glacier; chances of landslides and ice avalanches at the wall to the right of the lake; one lake and two small lakes in the upper catchment
lakes.why_it_matters: Downstream of Langmale, which burst in 2017 from a Saldim Peak rockfall. The upper-catchment lakes flagged in the PDGL note are exactly the mass-flow-into-lake case Stage 4 must detect.
lakes.coordinate_source: ICIMOD/UNDP 2020 PDGL report, lake ID GL087092E27798N

lakes.name: Chamlang (South)
lakes.pdgl_note: Hanging glaciers; high chance of ice avalanches; lake formation near the end moraine; ice underneath the dam; small ponds on the dam, but the dam is more than 500 m long
lakes.why_it_matters: Rank II rather than I, so it tests whether the hazard ranking discriminates within the PDGL list, not just PDGL vs non-PDGL.
lakes.coordinate_source: ICIMOD/UNDP 2020 PDGL report, lake ID GL086958E27755N

lakes.name: Lumding
lakes.pdgl_note: Lake expanding rapidly, in contact with calving glacier; three hanging lakes in the side valley; continuous dam slope
lakes.why_it_matters: The PDGL nearest to Thyanbo, 5.8 km away. Its presence on the 2020 list while Thyanbo is absent is the sharpest possible statement of the blind spot.
lakes.coordinate_source: ICIMOD/UNDP 2020 PDGL report, lake ID GL086612E27779N

lakes.name: Hongu 1
lakes.pdgl_note: Lake expanding towards the retreating glacier snout; hanging lakes on both sides of the valley; lake outlet close to the dam end; many cascading lakes in the lower old moraine
lakes.why_it_matters: Cascading-lake configuration, the same chain-reaction geometry that produced the two-stage Thame failure.
lakes.coordinate_source: ICIMOD/UNDP 2020 PDGL report, lake ID GL086935E27838N

lakes.name: Hongu 2
lakes.pdgl_note: Hanging glacier; chances of avalanches; short dam length; steep slope with many erosional features
lakes.why_it_matters: Explicit hanging-glacier avalanche risk, a direct test of the Stage 4 ice-avalanche source-slope proxy (45-60 deg on glacierized terrain).
lakes.coordinate_source: ICIMOD/UNDP 2020 PDGL report, lake ID GL086957E27783N

lakes.name: Gokyo Cho / Dudh Pokhari
lakes.why_it_matters: Large, well-known, stable, NOT in contact with a mother glacier and NOT PDGL-listed. A true negative that a naive area-threshold screen would wrongly flag on size alone: the false-positive test.

lakes.name: Tilicho Lake
lakes.why_it_matters: Large high-altitude glacial lake, stable, not PDGL-listed, in the Gandaki basin. Second false-positive test, and geographically separated from the Koshi cluster.
